retrained_donor_doc58_SS16_2.why_retrained: doc 58 SS16.2, registered because it is easy to get wrong: the committed donor R1-W_s0 was trained on the FIRST draw's train split. scope_doc58_SS12: NO QUANTUM READING OF ANY KIND. The comparators are already at 1.0000 on both instances; there is nothing for a circuit to win. exp72 is about OPTIMISATION and only optimisation, and NO EXP72 NUMBER MAY APPEAR IN A SENTENCE CONTAINING 'ADVANTAGE'.

NOT A STATEMENT ABOUT BARREN PLATEAUS. These are 4-qubit circuits. No gradient-variance-versus-qubit-count scaling is measured, and doc 58 SS4.4 / SS4.5's asymptotic results are cited as MECHANISM LANGUAGE, never as diagnoses of these instances.

'THE FIELD'S MITIGATIONS' MEANS EXACTLY THESE FOUR OPERATIONALISATIONS, not the literature's every variant. Noted, not run: full barren-plateau-aware initialisation schemes (beta / Gaussian / reduced-domain / He / Xavier, and the CNN- and RL-based initialisers); quantum natural gradient; SGLD and other noisy/stochastic-gradient optimisers; encoding-entanglement reduction; cost-function locality; circuit-growing layerwise learning in Skolik et al.'s published form; the R-budget budget/schedule decomposition. A NULL ON THESE FOUR IS NOT A NULL ON THOSE.
One dataset, one task family, one category, one surface, two referents, two events, 24 nouns, simulation. doc 50 SS7's ceiling stands.

NOT 'MEANING', not composition-in-general, not DisCoCirc's expressive limits. A rescue relocates a failure from 'training' to 'training with a better recipe'; a null relocates nothing. Neither touches representability -- the bounds are 1.0000 in both cases and always were.
Not novel-filler generalisation; exp69's held-out-PAIRING split, inherited.
R-layerwise is an ADAPTATION of arXiv:2006.14904, not a replication (SS4.2). A null on it says NOTHING about their published circuit-growing method.
